===== ORIGINAL PROMPT (initial_prompt.md) =====
Build a polished, fully offline-first iOS voice-journaling app called
"Fieldnotes". Native Apple stack only: SwiftUI + SwiftData, AVFoundation
for recording, Speech framework for on-device transcription, Natural­
Language framework for on-device tagging/sentiment, PencilKit for sketch
annotations. No backend, no accounts, no network dependency for any core
feature — everything must work in airplane mode. Follow the
ios-app-factory-rules. If a requested capability needs something this
project genuinely cannot provide (a special Apple entitlement, a paid
developer account feature, server-side ML), do NOT fake or stub it —
record it as an explicit gap with what it would actually take.

Core features (complete over broad — ship fewer things fully working):

1. Voice entries: record audio journal entries with a live waveform
   view while recording. Recording must survive being interrupted by a
   phone call, Siri, or the app being backgrounded, and must resume
   or cleanly finalize the entry rather than corrupt/lose it — get
   AVAudioSession category/interruption handling genuinely right, this
   is the hardest technical part of the app.
2. On-device transcription: transcribe each recording using Speech
   framework (on-device recognition only — reject/flag if only
   server-based recognition is available for a locale). Transcript is
   editable after the fact; edits must not desync from the audio
   timeline (tapping a transcript sentence seeks the audio to that
   point).
3. Auto-tagging & mood: run NaturalLanguage tokenization/sentiment on
   each transcript to suggest tags and a mood score. Suggestions are
   editable/dismissible — never silently apply an AI guess as fact.
4. Sketch annotations: attach PencilKit sketches to any entry (finger
   or Pencil), stored alongside the audio/transcript.
5. Bi-directional linking: entries can @-mention/link other entries;
   each entry shows a "linked from" backlinks section computed live
   from the local store (no manual backlink maintenance) — same
   integrity discipline as a graph/notes app: linking, unlinking, and
   deleting an entry must never leave a dangling or duplicate backlink.
6. Search: full-text search across transcripts AND tags/mood, with
   results ranked by a real relevance score you define and document
   (not just substring match order).
7. HealthKit correlation (read-only, explicit permission): show each
   entry's mood alongside that day's HealthKit sleep/activity summary
   if authorized, and degrade to "not connected" honestly if denied —
   never block core journaling on this permission.
8. Home-screen widget + Live Activity: widget shows the latest entry's
   mood/snippet; a Live Activity shows elapsed time and live waveform
   while actively recording, ending cleanly when the recording stops
   or the app is killed mid-recording (no orphaned Live Activity).
9. Share Extension (separate target): accept shared text or a photo
   from other apps and create a new Fieldnotes entry from it.
10. App Intents: "Start a voice entry" and "Search my journal" exposed
    to Shortcuts/Siri.
11. CarPlay: a minimal CarPlay scene for hands-free start/stop
    recording while driving. This requires Apple's CarPlay audio-app
    entitlement, which a personal free developer account cannot
    obtain — if that's confirmed true in this environment, build the
    CarPlay scene code path correctly but record in Gaps that it
    cannot actually run/ship without that entitlement, rather than
    silently omitting the feature or pretending it works.

Priorities, in order: (a) audio-session interruption correctness — a
lost or corrupted recording is the worst possible failure, (b) backlink
graph integrity, (c) honest degradation of every permission-gated
feature (Speech, HealthKit, CarPlay). Use Decimal/Int for anything
numeric that isn't inherently floating (durations in seconds as
TimeInterval is fine; don't invent unnecessary Decimal use here — this
app's money-precision lesson from prior apps doesn't apply, there's no
currency). Seed a "demo entries" toggle in Settings with realistic
sample entries, transcripts, tags, and backlinks so no screen is empty
on first review. Provide a clear way to run it in the iOS Simulator via
Xcode, and call out anywhere CarPlay/HealthKit/Speech behave differently
in Simulator vs. a real device.

===== PHASE PLAYBOOK (editable phase_rules.json) =====
Global app-build rules:
- Prefer a smaller finished app over a larger half-built app.
- Every generated app must have real user-visible behavior, not only placeholder screens.
- For iOS apps, default to SwiftUI, deterministic local state first, Apple system frameworks, and no third-party package unless it materially reduces risk.
- Every screen needs empty, loading, success, and error states when the workflow can reach those states.
- No two text or control elements may visually overlap, collide, or clip each other. Labels never sit on top of values; values never stack into each other. When elements are positioned by a data value (times on a timeline, points on an axis), enforce a minimum gap and de-clutter (offset, group, collapse, or drop a colliding label) — overlapping text is a broken screen.
- The interface must never claim an outcome that has not happened: show Saved/Deleted/Sent/Synced/Unlocked only after it is truly confirmed, never a success state shown unconditionally. No sample or placeholder data shown as if it were the user's real data.
- Implement the design spec's tokens as one SwiftUI theme file (e.g. Theme.swift with type, spacing, and color definitions) and reference it everywhere; never scatter font/size/color literals through views.
- Every generated app must fully support dark mode: semantic color roles with explicit light and dark values, verified in both appearances.
- Empty states are designed content (icon + one-line explanation + the action that fills the screen), never a blank view or bare 'No data' text.
- No default unstyled List, Form, or navigation chrome where the design spec calls for custom rows, cards, or backgrounds; the built UI must match the spec.
- Treat accessibility, privacy, persistence, and testing as product requirements, not polish.
- Do not declare the app done until build verification and the final review agree on what works and what remains limited.

Phase rules:
- Preserve the user's original prompt before interpreting it.
- Convert the prompt into hard requirements, non-goals, output shape, quality bar, and decision rules.
- Resolve conflicts by naming the assumption, not by silently changing the assignment.

Required output:
- Original prompt excerpt or full prompt reference.
- Hard requirements.
- Non-goals.
- Production-readiness definition.
- Decision rules for later phases.
- A NUMBERED list of testable requirements extracted from the user's prompt — each one verifiable by using the app.

Acceptance checks before consensus:
- A later phase can tell whether it is violating the user's prompt.
- Multi-app quantity/category requirements are explicit.
- Production-ready means more than a prototype or spec.
- Every promise in the original prompt maps to a numbered requirement; nothing is silently dropped.


===== RELEVANT KNOWLEDGE (curated IOS reference — use it, don't restate it) =====

----- Apple Frameworks Cheatsheet -----
# First-Party Apple Frameworks Cheatsheet (iOS 17+ / Swift 5.9+)

Build capable iPhone apps with **zero third-party dependencies**. For each framework: when to reach for it, the entry-point type, and a compilable, idiomatic snippet or the gotcha that bites people. All examples target **iOS 17 minimum** unless a call-out says otherwise; Swift Concurrency (`async`/`await`) is preferred over completion handlers everywhere Apple offers it.

## General rules

- **Prefer these over SPM packages.** RevenueCat, Firebase Analytics, Lottie, Alamofire, etc. all have first-party equivalents good enough for most apps. Fewer deps = smaller binary, faster builds, no supply-chain risk, no privacy-manifest surprises.
- **Every framework that touches user data needs an `Info.plist` usage-description string** (or an entitlement). Missing it is a runtime crash the moment the API is used — not a compile error. The specific keys are listed per section.
- **Import the framework and its SwiftUI companion when one exists** (e.g. `import MapKit` gives you `Map`; `import StoreKit` gives you `SubscriptionStoreView`/`StoreView`).
- **Do capability checks before hardware-dependent APIs** (`CHHapticEngine.capabilitiesForHardware().supportsHaptics`, `HKHealthStore.isHealthDataAvailable()`, `GKLocalPlayer.local.isAuthenticated`). Simulators and older/cheaper devices lie.
- **Never block the main actor.** Long queries, audio-graph setup, and StoreKit calls belong in `Task {}` or `async` functions.
- **Verify APIs against the deployment target.** Several SwiftUI conveniences (e.g. `GameCenterView`, Control widgets) shipped *after* iOS 17. Availability call-outs below flag these.

---

## StoreKit 2 — In-App Purchase & Subscriptions

**Use it when:** you sell anything — consumables, non-consumables, or auto-renewable subscriptions. Replaces callback-based StoreKit 1 entirely.

**Start from:** `Product` (fetch + purchase) and `Transaction` (entitlements + history). No server strictly required — signatures are verified on-device via `VerificationResult`.

### The three things you must do

1. **Load products by ID** (IDs come from App Store Connect):

```swift
import StoreKit

let productIDs = ["com.app.pro.monthly", "com.app.pro.yearly", "com.app.coins.100"]
let products = try await Product.products(for: productIDs)   // async throws
```

2. **Purchase, then verify and finish the transaction:**

```swift
func purchase(_ product: Product) async throws -> Transaction? {
    let result = try await product.purchase()
    switch result {
    case .success(let verification):
        let transaction = try checkVerified(verification)
        await transaction.finish()          // REQUIRED — unfinished txns replay forever
        return transaction
    case .userCancelled, .pending:
        return nil
    @unknown default:
        return nil
    }
}

func checkVerified<T>(_ result: VerificationResult<T>) throws -> T {
    switch result {
    case .unverified(_, let error): throw error   // signature failed — do NOT grant
    case .verified(let safe):       return safe
    }
}
```

3. **Listen for `Transaction.updates` from app launch** — the single most-missed requirement. It catches renewals, Ask-to-Buy approvals, refunds, and purchases made on other devices.

```swift
// Start this in your App init / a top-level task and keep it alive for the app's lifetime.
func observeTransactions() -> Task<Void, Never> {
    Task.detached {
        for await update in Transaction.updates {
            guard case .verified(let transaction) = update else { continue }
            await grantEntitlement(for: transaction)   // your unlock logic
            await transaction.finish()
        }
    }
}
```

### Checking what the user currently owns

Use `Transaction.currentEntitlements` (an async sequence). **iOS 18.4+ note:** the per-product `Transaction.currentEntitlement(for:)` is deprecated in favor of `Transaction.currentEntitlements(for:)`, because a user can hold multiple entitling transactions (e.g. own it *and* have Family Sharing access).

```swift
func hasActiveSubscription() async -> Bool {
    for await result in Transaction.currentEntitlements {
        guard case .verified(let transaction) = result else { continue }
        if transaction.productType == .autoRenewable && transaction.revocationDate == nil {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}
```

### Subscription status & renewal info

```swift
// groupID = the subscription group configured in App Store Connect
let statuses = try await Product.SubscriptionInfo.status(for: subscriptionGroupID)
for status in statuses {
    guard case .verified(let renewalInfo) = status.renewalInfo else { continue }
    let willAutoRenew = renewalInfo.willAutoRenew   // false => user cancelled, still in period
    _ = (status.state, willAutoRenew)               // .subscribed, .expired, .inGracePeriod, ...
}
```

### Drop-in SwiftUI storefront (iOS 17+)

Skip building a custom paywall — these render Apple's native UI:

```swift
import SwiftUI
import StoreKit

// Whole subscription group with a marketing header:
SubscriptionStoreView(groupID: subscriptionGroupID) {
    VStack { Text("Unlock Pro").font(.largeTitle.bold()) }
}
.subscriptionStoreControlStyle(.prominentPicker)

// Non-subscription products:
StoreView(ids: ["com.app.coins.100", "com.app.coins.500"])
```

### Gotchas

- **Test locally with a `.storekit` configuration file** (Xcode → File → New → File → StoreKit Configuration). Lets you buy, refund, and fast-forward renewals in the simulator with no sandbox account.
- `await transaction.finish()` is mandatory — forgetting it makes the transaction reappear in `Transaction.updates` every launch.
- **Always ship a "Restore Purchases" button** for non-consumables/subscriptions (App Review requirement). Call `try await AppStore.sync()`, then re-scan `currentEntitlements`.
- **Consumables are not in `currentEntitlements`** — grant them at p

This phase contract turns that into execution terms:
The product exists for one user value: a private, offline-first voice + text + sketch journaling experience that stays reliable under real-world interruptions and remains meaningfully reviewable over time via links, transcription, and lightweight analytics. The high-commitment version is a focused local-first graph-aware journaling system, not a social/socially-networked diary tool.

Hard requirements:
- Target AppKit-incompatible: iOS native only, using SwiftUI, SwiftData, AVFoundation, Speech, NaturalLanguage, PencilKit, and system-first extensions/features. No third-party services or backend dependencies for core behavior.
- Offline-first is absolute for journaling, recording, transcribing, tagging, search, and linking; airplane mode should not block primary tasks.
- Implement all required targets/features unless blocked by platform entitlement; if blocked, ship explicit, user-visible gap notes instead of fake behavior.
- Prioritize audio correctness above feature breadth, with interruption-safe recording as the top guardrail.
- Use the app as a single source of truth persisted locally with SwiftData and a deliberate lifecycle model for recordings, transcripts, tags, sketches, and links.
- Ensure explicit permission-gated behavior for Speech and HealthKit where denial is an allowed branch that preserves core journaling.
- Expose and test realistic sample data through Settings through a one-step "seed demo entries" action, not hidden defaults.
- Deliver visual and behavioral states for empty/loading/success/error where they can occur.
- Use one shared design token/theme implementation and keep behavior honest: never report saved/deleted/synced before confirmation.
- Respect dark mode and avoid visual collisions and overlap.

Non-goals:
- No cloud sync, account systems, or remote shared journals.
- No server-side transcription or paid API fallback for core flow.
- No pretending entitlement-locked features run in environments where they cannot.
- No currency/financial precision subsystem or unrelated analytics pipeline.
- No “always-on AI truth”: tags/moods are suggestions only.

Success metrics (production-readiness testable):
- Zero data loss on tested interruption scenarios (Siri, call, background, force-quit after stop) across 20+ manual runs.
- 100% of editable transcripts maintain alignment points; seeking by sentence always maps to an existing audio timestamp.
- Backlink graph checks pass on create/update/delete cycles with no duplicates, no missing reverse links, and no dangling references.
- Permission degradation paths for Speech and HealthKit remain usable and non-blocking, with clear user-facing status.
- Search returns consistent ranking under repeated queries for same corpus (no random order).
- Build includes all explicit targets: app, widget, live activity, intent extension, share extension, CarPlay code path.
- Simulator run documentation exists, including known simulator-only differences and limitations.

Production-readiness definition:
Production-ready means: crash-avoidant default behavior across target OS features, complete local persistence and recovery semantics for recording/transcript/link/tag/sketch data, deterministic permission handling, testable interruption path, and explicit gap documentation for anything blocked by environment limits. A feature is considered ready only if it has implemented behavior, visible states, and clear failure handling; not placeholders and not unverified “works in theory” code. It must survive realistic use within iOS lifecycle constraints and be installable/run via Xcode in Simulator with a clear launch path.

Decision rules for later phases:
- Preserve prompt order and intent exactly. If constraints conflict, do not silently reinterpret; escalate as an explicit decision and choose the least risky interpretation that keeps core user value.
- Any uncertain platform capability (entitlement, locale availability, simulator mismatch) must become an explicit gap note with “what is blocked, why, and required remedy.”
- If a feature can be implemented with honest fallback, do that immediately; only then mark as “completed with degraded mode.” If it cannot, mark as “gapped” with actionable remediation.
- Never use fake data to simulate real data integrity, especially for state like saved/deleted/linked counts and search results.
- Every requirement below maps to one or more tests that can be manually exercised in-app and checked off before considering a phase complete.
- If implementation deviates from this contract, document the deviation in the backlog with impact and replacement behavior.

Testable requirements:
1. The app is called Fieldnotes and is implemented in SwiftUI + SwiftData with zero core-network dependency.
2. Audio entry recording starts, captures waveform continuously while recording, and writes audio to local storage in a durable, non-corrupt state.
3. Interruption handling recovers correctly when a phone call, Siri event, or backgrounding occurs: recording is either resumed safely or finalized cleanly without corruption.
4. AVAudioSession category/activation/interruption handling is implemented and observable through app behavior during interruption transitions.
5. Each recording has an associated transcript generated via Speech framework and does not silently use server-only recognition for a locale that is not on-device capable.
6. If on-device recognition is unavailable, the user sees explicit flagging and no false claim of on-device completion.
7. Transcript editing is supported after recording, with stable sentence-to-time mapping so taps seek to the matching audio moment.
8. Transcript edits do not break later playback alignment.
9. NaturalLanguage analysis runs on transcript content and generates mood plus suggested tags.
10. Suggested tags/mood are user-editable, dismissible, and never auto-finalized without user confirmation.
11. PencilKit annotations can be attached per entry using Apple Pencil or finger, and persist with the entry.
12. Entries can @-mention/link other entries in text, and backlinks are computed live from the local store.
13. Creating, deleting, and unlinking entries never produces dangling or duplicate backlinks.
14. Search covers transcript text, tag values, and mood and returns ranked results based on a documented relevance score formula.
15. Search results are reproducible for identical queries and ranking logic.
16. HealthKit read permission can be requested explicitly; on grant, entries show per-day sleep/activity context aligned to entry date.
17. On HealthKit denial, journaling remains fully usable and UI shows honest “not connected.”
18. Home-screen widget displays latest entry mood and snippet.
19. Live Activity appears while recording, shows elapsed time and live waveform, and terminates cleanly on stop or app kill with no orphaned activity.
20. Share extension accepts incoming text or photo and creates a Fieldnotes entry.
21. App Intents expose “Start a voice entry” and “Search my journal” and run without backend dependencies.
22. CarPlay scene allows hands-free start/stop flow in code, with explicit gap documentation if entitlement is unavailable in this environment.
23. Settings includes a demo-entries toggle that seeds realistic data and ensures no first-run screen is empty.
24. App follows dark-mode semantics with design tokens centralized in one theme file and consistent styling usage across screens.
25. All user-facing screens implement empty/loading/success/error states when those states are possible.
26. No placeholder states claim completed real user actions or fake completed transactions.
27. A run guide for Xcode simulator setup is included, with explicit notes on known simulator vs device behavior differences for Speech, HealthKit, Live Activity, and CarPlay.
28. Numeric values are represented with Int/Decimal only where appropriate; avoid unnecessary Decimal for non-money values.

Biggest objective-risk objection I see is over-ambition across platform surfaces. The direction is to prioritize a brutally reliable recording core and graph integrity, then layer extensions; this keeps the product remarkable by being trustworthy before it is broad. The highest integrity detail this contract must preserve is the interruption model and the integrity rule for links—if either fails, the app is not production-ready regardless of optional feature count.

----- Apple Frameworks Cheatsheet -----
# First-Party Apple Frameworks Cheatsheet (iOS 17+ / Swift 5.9+)

Build capable iPhone apps with **zero third-party dependencies**. For each framework: when to reach for it, the entry-point type, and a compilable, idiomatic snippet or the gotcha that bites people. All examples target **iOS 17 minimum** unless a call-out says otherwise; Swift Concurrency (`async`/`await`) is preferred over completion handlers everywhere Apple offers it.

## General rules

- **Prefer these over SPM packages.** RevenueCat, Firebase Analytics, Lottie, Alamofire, etc. all have first-party equivalents good enough for most apps. Fewer deps = smaller binary, faster builds, no supply-chain risk, no privacy-manifest surprises.
- **Every framework that touches user data needs an `Info.plist` usage-description string** (or an entitlement). Missing it is a runtime crash the moment the API is used — not a compile error. The specific keys are listed per section.
- **Import the framework and its SwiftUI companion when one exists** (e.g. `import MapKit` gives you `Map`; `import StoreKit` gives you `SubscriptionStoreView`/`StoreView`).
- **Do capability checks before hardware-dependent APIs** (`CHHapticEngine.capabilitiesForHardware().supportsHaptics`, `HKHealthStore.isHealthDataAvailable()`, `GKLocalPlayer.local.isAuthenticated`). Simulators and older/cheaper devices lie.
- **Never block the main actor.** Long queries, audio-graph setup, and StoreKit calls belong in `Task {}` or `async` functions.
- **Verify APIs against the deployment target.** Several SwiftUI conveniences (e.g. `GameCenterView`, Control widgets) shipped *after* iOS 17. Availability call-outs below flag these.

---

## StoreKit 2 — In-App Purchase & Subscriptions

**Use it when:** you sell anything — consumables, non-consumables, or auto-renewable subscriptions. Replaces callback-based StoreKit 1 entirely.

**Start from:** `Product` (fetch + purchase) and `Transaction` (entitlements + history). No server strictly required — signatures are verified on-device via `VerificationResult`.

### The three things you must do

1. **Load products by ID** (IDs come from App Store Connect):

```swift
import StoreKit

let productIDs = ["com.app.pro.monthly", "com.app.pro.yearly", "com.app.coins.100"]
let products = try await Product.products(for: productIDs)   // async throws
```

2. **Purchase, then verify and finish the transaction:**

```swift
func purchase(_ product: Product) async throws -> Transaction? {
    let result = try await product.purchase()
    switch result {
    case .success(let verification):
        let transaction = try checkVerified(verification)
        await transaction.finish()          // REQUIRED — unfinished txns replay forever
        return transaction
    case .userCancelled, .pending:
        return nil
    @unknown default:
        return nil
    }
}

func checkVerified<T>(_ result: VerificationResult<T>) throws -> T {
    switch result {
    case .unverified(_, let error): throw error   // signature failed — do NOT grant
    case .verified(let safe):       return safe
    }
}
```

3. **Listen for `Transaction.updates` from app launch** — the single most-missed requirement. It catches renewals, Ask-to-Buy approvals, refunds, and purchases made on other devices.

```swift
// Start this in your App init / a top-level task and keep it alive for the app's lifetime.
func observeTransactions() -> Task<Void, Never> {
    Task.detached {
        for await update in Transaction.updates {
            guard case .verified(let transaction) = update else { continue }
            await grantEntitlement(for: transaction)   // your unlock logic
            await transaction.finish()
        }
    }
}
```

### Checking what the user currently owns

Use `Transaction.currentEntitlements` (an async sequence). **iOS 18.4+ note:** the per-product `Transaction.currentEntitlement(for:)` is deprecated in favor of `Transaction.currentEntitlements(for:)`, because a user can hold multiple entitling transactions (e.g. own it *and* have Family Sharing access).

```swift
func hasActiveSubscription() async -> Bool {
    for await result in Transaction.currentEntitlements {
        guard case .verified(let transaction) = result else { continue }
        if transaction.productType == .autoRenewable && transaction.revocationDate == nil {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}
```

### Subscription status & renewal info

```swift
// groupID = the subscription group configured in App Store Connect
let statuses = try await Product.SubscriptionInfo.status(for: subscriptionGroupID)
for status in statuses {
    guard case .verified(let renewalInfo) = status.renewalInfo else { continue }
    let willAutoRenew = renewalInfo.willAutoRenew   // false => user cancelled, still in period
    _ = (status.state, willAutoRenew)               // .subscribed, .expired, .inGracePeriod, ...
}
```

### Drop-in SwiftUI storefront (iOS 17+)

Skip building a custom paywall — these render Apple's native UI:

```swift
import SwiftUI
import StoreKit

// Whole subscription group with a marketing header:
SubscriptionStoreView(groupID: subscriptionGroupID) {
    VStack { Text("Unlock Pro").font(.largeTitle.bold()) }
}
.subscriptionStoreControlStyle(.prominentPicker)

// Non-subscription products:
StoreView(ids: ["com.app.coins.100", "com.app.coins.500"])
```

### Gotchas

- **Test locally with a `.storekit` configuration file** (Xcode → File → New → File → StoreKit Configuration). Lets you buy, refund, and fast-forward renewals in the simulator with no sandbox account.
- `await transaction.finish()` is mandatory — forgetting it makes the transaction reappear in `Transaction.updates` every launch.
- **Always ship a "Restore Purchases" button** for non-consumables/subscriptions (App Review requirement). Call `try await AppStore.sync()`, then re-scan `currentEntitlements`.

The product exists for one user value: a private, offline-first voice + text + sketch journaling experience that stays reliable under real-world interruptions and remains meaningfully reviewable over time via links, transcription, and lightweight analytics. Hard requirements:

Production-ready means: crash-avoidant default behavior across target OS features, complete local persistence and recovery semantics for recording/transcript/link/tag/sketch data, deterministic permission handling, testable interruption path, and explicit gap documentation for anything blocked by environment limits. A feature is considered ready only if it has implemented behavior, visible states, and clear failure handling; not placeholders and not unverified “works in theory” code.
